cards.headline: The quiet duo's one dance song
cards.snippet: Kings of Convenience — Bergen's Erlend Øye and Eirik Glambek Bøe — made their name with hush: two voices, two guitars, songs that never raise their voice. 'I'd Rather Dance with You' is the great exception: track eight on their second album, Riot on an Empty Street (released 21 June 2004), a bright, bouncing plea to skip the conversation and move into the other room. Issued as the album's second single on 23 August 2004, it reached No. 65 in the UK — while the album around it climbed to No. 2 in Norway and No. 3 in Italy, where it stayed on the chart for a year.
cards.context: Feist sings on two of the album's other tracks — 'Know-How' and 'The Build-Up' — but the dance song is the duo alone.

cards.headline: The video MTV Europe called 2004's best
cards.snippet: The song's fame rides on its video: Øye — tall, bespectacled, tracksuit-clad — throws himself into a children's dance class with total commitment and no technique at all, and wins the room by sheer joy. MTV Europe named it the best music video of 2004. Uploaded to YouTube in 2009, it has passed 18 million views, and the algorithm keeps delivering it to new listeners, who arrive in its comments by the thousand to report the same discovery: it is almost impossible to watch without moving.
cards.context: Regulars have been identifying the extras for years — Bøe's wife Ina can be spotted in the audience near the end, around the 3:13 mark.

cards.headline: Sherlock and Frodo, it turns out, can sing
cards.snippet: I had no idea that Sherlock and Frodo could sing like this.
cards.context: The comparison is the thread's favourite joke: Øye as Benedict Cumberbatch, Bøe as Elijah Wood — and this is its most-liked telling.

replies.author: @ariellemroberts
replies.text: lol I actually thought it was Frodo until i looked really closely. I'm here like, "He actually sings?"

replies.author: @gma7033
replies.text: He looks like the son of Frodo and Faramir

cards.headline: He sang 'Redemption Song' to us in an empty bar
cards.snippet: I met Erlend. he sang to me and my best friend in a empty bar, he sang the redemption song by bob marley. I didn't know who he was at the time.. when I found out I flipped out. was an amazing moment
cards.context: The replies answer with an Erlend story of their own: asked for a paid lift, he turned it down with 'Ok, I still like you.'

replies.author: @ragnarkisten
replies.text: Erlend once asked me if I could drive him somewhere, and that he would pay for it. I told him no, didn't want to leave my buddies. "Ok, I still like you," he replied.

replies.author: @jasonruiz5401
replies.text: Ya, one time I was flying on an eagle, and I just happened to see Erlend fighting a zebra over some flip flops. I told him I had an extra pair but he was like, no thanks bro.

cards.headline: The algorithm's favourite old song
cards.snippet: No one: YouTube: listen to this song from 2009
cards.context: The replies supply the correction: the song is from 2004 — 2009 is only when Vevo uploaded the video to YouTube.

replies.author: @toddmichaeljohnson7139
replies.text: It’s 2019 and heard this song for the first time yesterday. Been listening nonstop since! 10 years late to this gem 💎

cards.headline: A thank-you note to a clicking finger
cards.snippet: I will forever thank my finger for clicking on this video
cards.context: Its most-liked reply adds the credential the joke leaves out: the video that finger found won MTV Europe's best video.

replies.author: @alinevargasrodriguez8579
replies.text: In fact this video win ''best european video'' by mtv, this norway guys are awesomes

replies.author: @kasmene74
replies.text: I  hope girls too for using that finger! :D

cards.headline: Pomplamoose (2019): a favourite covering a favourite
cards.snippet: Pomplamoose — Nataly Dawn and Jack Conte's duo — recorded their cover in February 2019 at Redstar Recording in Los Angeles, with a full band around Conte's keys; the video has passed 480,000 views. One listener: "The tamborine/crash cymbal at 2:47 was appreciated by Jack. I love those little moments."
cards.context: The cover's thread is a crossover crowd — one listener calls it 'my favorite covering my favorite.'

version.versionLabel: I'd Rather Dance With You | Kings of Convenience Cover

cards.headline: Le Bataclan, 2009: Feist joins the dance
cards.snippet: Five years after the album, the duo played Le Bataclan in Paris on 11 November 2009 — and Feist, who sings on the album's other singles, joined them for this one; a fan's film of it has passed 159,000 views. One listener: "Wait. Shouldn't it be "i'd rather dance with someone else"? 😂"
cards.context: On the album, Feist sings the quiet duets — 'Know-How' and 'The Build-Up' — so her turn on the dance song is the evening's twist, and the thread knows it.

version.versionLabel: Live at Le Bataclan, Paris — 11 November 2009
